'''Zhenan Bao''' ({{lang-zh|s=鲍哲南|t=|p=Bào Zhé-nán}}; born 1970) is a Chinese-born American chemical engineer. She serves as K. K. Lee Professor of Chemical Engineering at [[Stanford University]], with courtesy appointments in Chemistry and Material Science and Engineering.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Zhenan Bao {{!}} Chemical Engineering|url=https://cheme.stanford.edu/person/zhenan-bao|access-date=22 May 2021|website=cheme.stanford.edu|language=en|archive-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522195457/https://cheme.stanford.edu/person/zhenan-bao|url-status=dead}}</ref> She served as the Department Chair of Chemical Engineering from 2018 to 2022.<ref name=":0" /> She was an Associate Editor for the Royal Society of Chemistry journal Chemical Science, Polymer Reviews and Synthetic Metals. Bao is known for her work on [[organic field-effect transistor]]s and [[organic semiconductors]], for applications including [[flexible electronics]] and [[electronic skin]].

==Early life and education==
Bao was born in [[Nanjing|Nanjing, China]] in 1970.<ref name="C&EN rising stars">{{cite news|last=MacDermott|first=Kevin|date=25 March 2002|title=TAKING AN EARLY LEAD|newspaper=C&EN|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/women/8012/8012bus4.html|access-date=23 February 2013}}</ref> She is the daughter of a professor of physical chemistry at [[Nanjing University]].<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Interview: Great expectations – Chemical Science Blog|url=https://blogs.rsc.org/sc/2010/08/31/interview-great-expectations/|access-date=22 May 2021|language=en-US}}</ref>

Bao studied chemistry as an undergraduate student at Nanjing University beginning in 1987.<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /> While at Nanjing University, she worked in the laboratory of Gi Xue on gold [[cross-link]]ed [[polymer]]s.<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Xue|first1=Gi|last2=Wu|first2=Peiyi|last3=Bao|first3=Zhenan|last4=Dong|first4=Jian|last5=Cheng|first5=Rongshi|date=1 January 1990|title=Air-oxidation of gold metal in polybenzimidazole solution|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1990/c3/c39900000495|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications|language=en|issue=6|pages=495–497|doi=10.1039/C39900000495|issn=0022-4936|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 1990, Bao moved to the [[United States]] with her family, enrolling in the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] as she had family nearby.<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /><ref name=":1" /> Several months later, Bao was accepted directly into the PhD program in chemistry at the [[The University of Chicago|University of Chicago]] without a bachelor's degree, owing to two awards she won while an undergraduate at Nanjing University.<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Zhenan Bao – Zhenan Bao Research Group at Stanford Chemical 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127090704/https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/zbao|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the University of Chicago, as one of the first graduate students of Bao received a [[Master of Science]] in chemistry in 1993 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in chemistry in 1995, both from the University of Chicago. To this day, she does not hold any bachelor's degrees.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zhenan Bao's Profile {{!}} Stanford Profiles |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/zhenan-bao |access-date=2023-04-18 |website=profiles.stanford.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon the completion of her doctorate, Bao received an offer to join the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a postdoctoral scholar, but instead chose to join the Materials Research Department at [[Bell Labs]] of [[Lucent Technologies]].<ref name=":1" /> At Bell Labs, she developed the first all-plastic transistor, or [[organic field-effect transistor]], which allows for use in electronic paper.<ref name="C&EN Bell Labs">{{cite news|last=Dagani|first=Ron|title=AN INNOVATION ENGINE FOR LUCENT|url=http://pubs.acs.org/isubscribe/journals/cen/76/i48/html/7648scit11.html|access-date=23 February 2013|newspaper=C&EN|date=30 November 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Bao|first=Zhenan|author2=Dodabalapur, Ananth |author3=Lovinger, Andrew J. |title=Soluble and processable regioregular poly(3-hexylthiophene) for thin film field-effect transistor applications with high mobility|journal=Applied Physics Letters|date=1 January 1996|volume=69|issue=26|pages=4108|doi=10.1063/1.117834|bibcode=1996ApPhL..69.4108B}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Bao|first=Zhenan|author2=Feng, Yi |author3=Dodabalapur, Ananth |author4=Raju, V. R. |author5= Lovinger, Andrew J. |title=High-Performance Plastic Transistors Fabricated by Printing Techniques|journal=Chemistry of Materials|date=1 June 1997|volume=9|issue=6|pages=1299–1301|doi=10.1021/cm9701163}}</ref> It was also during this time when [[Schön scandal|Jan Hendrik Schön]] published a series of papers claiming major breakthroughs involving semiconductors, two of which included Bao as a coauthor. Schön's papers were ultimately retracted due to fraud, but Bao was cleared of allegations of misconduct.<ref name="Schon Fraud">{{cite news|last=Wilson|first=Elizabeth|title=Molecular Electronics: Schön's Fraud|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/89/i51/Molecular-Electronics-Schns-Fraud.html|access-date=23 February 2013|newspaper=C&EN|date=19 December 2011}}</ref> She was named a Distinguished Member of Technical Staff at Bell Labs in 2001.<ref name=":0" /> She founded the Stanford Wearable Electronics Initiative (eWEAR) and is the current faculty director.

In 2004, she returned to academia by joining the faculty at [[Stanford University]] where she is now focusing on studying [[organic semiconductor]] and [[carbon nanotubes]] using new fabrication methods. Recent work in the lab includes developing electronic skin<ref>{{cite news|last=Arnaud|first=Celia|title=Electronic Skin Heals Itself|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i47/Electronic-Skin-Heals-Itself.html|access-date=23 February 2013|newspaper=C&EN|date=19 November 2012}}</ref> and all-carbon solar cells.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ramuz|first=Marc P.|author2=Vosgueritchian, Michael |author3=Wei, Peng |author4=Wang, Chenggong |author5=Gao, Yongli |author6=Wu, Yingpeng |author7=Chen, Yongsheng |author8= Bao, Zhenan |title=Evaluation of Solution-Processable Carbon-Based Electrodes for All-Carbon Solar Cells|journal=ACS Nano|date=27 November 2012|volume=6|issue=11|pages=10384–10395|doi=10.1021/nn304410w|pmid=23113673}}</ref> Bao is a co-founder and on the board of directors for C3 Nano<ref>{{Cite web|title=Board of Directors|url=https://c3nano.com/about/board-of-directors/|access-date=22 May 2021|website=C3Nano|language=en-US|archive-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522195457/https://c3nano.com/about/board-of-directors/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and PyrAmes Health,<ref>{{Cite web|title=About PyrAmes – Vital data, innovative care.|url=https://pyrameshealth.com/our-company/|access-date=22 May 2021|website=PyrAmes|language=en-US}}</ref> both of which are [[Silicon Valley]] [[Venture capital|venture-funded]] [[Startup company|startup companies]]. She serves as an advising Partner for Fusion Venture Capital.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://c3nano.com/4318-2/|title = Zhenan Bao Receives l'Oreal-UNESCO 2017 Women in Science Intl. Award in 'Physical Sciences'|date = 12 November 2016|access-date = 23 September 2020|archive-date = 17 April 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210417132815/https://c3nano.com/4318-2/|url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/zbao|title=Zhenan Bao – Zhenan Bao Research Group at Stanford Chemical Engineering|access-date=23 September 2020|archive-date=14 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514063636/http://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/zbao|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bao and her team of researchers at Stanford University have several current projects in her research group as of 2022. Utilizing a “newly created printing method”, Bao and her team have developed skin-like integrated circuits. This new material can be used for “on-skin sensors, body-scale networks and implantable bioelectronics.” The process used for developing these materials is known as photolithography which, when combined with novel photochemistries, can generate the flexible materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New chemistry enables using existing technology to print stretchable, bendable circuits on artificial skin – Zhenan Bao Research Group at Stanford Chemical Engineering |url=https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/research-highlights/633-new-chemistry-enables-using-existing-technology-to-print-stretchable-bendable-circuits-on-artificial-skin |access-date=2 March 2022 |website=baogroup.stanford.edu |archive-date=2 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302020557/https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/research-highlights/633-new-chemistry-enables-using-existing-technology-to-print-stretchable-bendable-circuits-on-artificial-skin |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In conjunction with Karl Deisseroth, Bao has developed biocompatible polymers that can be used to “modulate the properties of target cells”. These cell-modulating biocompatible polymers alter certain properties of neurons and can either inhibit or boost neuronal firing. This technology can be used as a tool for exploration to better understand diseases such as multiple sclerosis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shayla |title=Stanford scientists program cells to carry out gene guided construction project – Zhenan Bao Research Group at Stanford Chemical Engineering |url=https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/research-highlights/629-stanford-scientists-program-cells-to-carry-out-gene-guided-construction-project |access-date=2 March 2022 |website=baogroup.stanford.edu |language=en-gb |archive-date=2 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302021038/https://baogroup.stanford.edu/index.php/research-highlights/629-stanford-scientists-program-cells-to-carry-out-gene-guided-construction-project |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
One of her major mentors was [[Elsa Reichmanis]], who was the department director at Bell Labs.<ref name="C&EN rising stars" /> She is married and has two children.<ref name="C&EN Rising Stars Reunite">{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Linda|title=Rising Stars Reunite|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/85/i41/Rising-Stars-Reunite.html|access-date=23 February 2013|newspaper=C&EN|date=8 October 2007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Walter|first=Patrick|title=Zhenan Bao: 'We just had to dream big'|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/culture/zhenan-bao-we-just-had-to-dream-big/4011280.article|access-date=22 May 2021|website=Chemistry World|language=en}}</ref>
